lesson.content:
## What it is
Logical (IP) and physical (MAC) addressing are two different types of addressing used in networking. Logical addressing, or IP addressing, is a 32-bit address assigned by the network and used by the network layer to reach hosts on any network. Physical addressing, or MAC addressing, is a 48-bit address burned into the network card and used inside one network by the data link layer. [p. 1]

## Real-life analogy
Think of IP addresses as a global phonebook where everyone has a unique number, while MAC addresses are like the stickers on your house that neighbors use to find you. [p. 1]

## How it works
1. **Logical (IP) Addressing**:
   - The network assigns a 32-bit IP address to each host, which is used by the network layer to reach hosts on any network. [p. 1]
   - This address is written in dotted decimal format, for example, 192.168.1.10. [p. 2]
   - IP addresses are divided into classes A, B, C, D (for multicast), and E (reserved). [p. 2]
2. **Physical (MAC) Addressing**:
   - Each host has a 48-bit MAC address burned into its network card. [p. 1]
   - This address is used by the data link layer to identify hosts within a single network. [p. 1]
   - MAC addresses are used in the frame header and change hop by hop, meaning they are different at each router. [p. 1]

## Key terms
- **Logical Address (IP Address)**: A 32-bit address used by the network layer to reach hosts on any network. [p. 2]
- **Physical Address (MAC Address)**: A 48-bit address burned into the network card and used by the data link layer. [p. 1]

## Example
Consider a network with two hosts, Host A with IP address 192.168.1.1 and Host B with IP address 192.168.1.2. Host A sends a packet to Host B. The packet will use the IP address 192.168.1.2 to reach Host B, regardless of the physical network it travels through. [p. 2]

## What to draw in the exam
- No diagram needed. [p. 1]

## Exam tip
Be able to distinguish between IP addresses and MAC addresses and understand their roles in the network. [p. 1]
